### COMPSCI 3TB3 / SFWRENG 4TB3 Syntax-Directed Tools and Compilers, 2025/26, McMaster University, Lab 10 & Assignment 10

**Emil Sekerinski (instructor), Brandon Bosman, Neel Joshi (TAs)**

Lab 10 is covered, and Assignment 10 is introduced at the following sessions:
- L01 on Wednesday, March 18
- L03 on Wednesday, March 18
- L04 on Friday, March 20
- L02 on Monday, March 23
- L05 on Monday, March 23

**Assignment 10 is due Tuesday, March 31, 11 pm \[24 points\].**
- You must work on this assignment on your own. You are encouraged to get a common understanding with fellow students, but the submission must be yours.
- You must not use LLMs like ChatGPT; likely, they wouldn't be of help anyway, but make you spend more time.
- The following week's labs present answers to the assignment questions.

The purpose of this lab is for you to
- understand common subexpression elimination, three-address code, basic blocks, and related notions of code optimization,
- understand that certain repetitions in source code may still be compiled efficiently, but some may not.

*Instructions:*
- Do not copy and paste graded cells, as that corrupts the notebook's metadata. You may add cells and copy the text of an existing cell into them, for example, to add test code or modify the given code. However, when the notebook is graded, all code is automatically executed from top to bottom, so you should remove or comment out extra code.
- Write answers to questions only in the graded text or code cells.
- Edit code only where it says YOUR CODE HERE; do not change the names of functions, methods, and classes; do not change the number or types of parameters; remove `raise NotImplementedError()`. Otherwise, the automatic grading fails, which may result in a deduction.
- Before submitting, "Restart Kernel" and run the notebook code from the top to clear the state of the kernel and to check that the output is as expected. When notebooks are graded, they are run with a freshly initialized kernel.
- Log files may be created when your program crashes. These log files may become so large that they prevent submission. Delete all log files and submit a cleaned-up folder.
- You are asked to write well-structured and readable source code. The source code is always used for grading in addition to the test results. Your program passing the provided tests does not guarantee that it is correct or that you will receive full (or any) marks.
